name: Pop-up Concert: Hub New Music
why: Monthly pop-up concert series featuring Hub New Music ensemble, running through December 1.

name: Changing Tastes: American Foodways at 250
why: Talk exploring 250 years of American food culture and culinary traditions.

name: La MaMa Puppet Festival 2026
why: Annual international puppet festival at La MaMa featuring companies from around the world; runs through December 6.

name: DOC NYC Film Festival
why: America's largest documentary festival; screenings at IFC Center, Village East, and other venues November 11–19.

name: Art Week NYC
why: Citywide art week with gallery openings, fairs, and special exhibitions; November 11–14.

name: Veterans Day Parade
why: Annual NYC Veterans Day Parade down 5th Avenue, the largest in the country.

name: Person Place Thing with Lili Taylor
why: Conversation and storytelling show hosted by Randy Cohen featuring actor Lili Taylor.

name: Fantastic Fiction at KGB
why: Monthly speculative fiction and fantasy reading series at KGB Bar.

name: Page Break: Stage Break Reading Series
why: Reading series featuring playwrights and prose writers performing their work.

name: Peer Revue
why: Scientists present peer-reviewed research to a live audience with humor and Q&A.

name: Central Chamber Series: Songs Without Words
why: Chamber music concert featuring Romantic and Modern repertoire for voice and piano without text.

name: Neue Galerie 25th Anniversary Exhibition
why: Special exhibition celebrating 25 years of the museum; opens November 12, runs through January 11, 2027.

name: Union Square Holiday Market
why: Annual outdoor holiday market at Union Square with hundreds of local vendors; November 12–December 24.

name: Broadway Under the Stars
why: Free weekly outdoor performances of Broadway numbers at Columbus Circle; weekly through December 17.

name: Modern Families: Expansive Depictions of Love
why: Panel discussion on how contemporary literature and media depict nontraditional family structures.

name: Who Owns the News?
why: Public discussion on media ownership, journalism economics, and the future of news.

name: Bad Movie Night: Ryan's Babe
why: Free screening of the cult disaster film Ryan's Babe (2001) with audience participation.

name: Domino Park Ice Skating
why: Seasonal outdoor ice skating rink at Domino Park; open through February 21, 2027.

name: The Standard High Line Ice Rink
why: Rooftop ice skating rink at The Standard High Line hotel; open through February 28, 2027.

name: Grand Central Holiday Fair
why: Annual holiday market inside Grand Central Terminal's Vanderbilt Hall; runs through December 24.

name: Big Apple Film Festival
why: Annual independent film festival running through November 12.

name: Westbeth Artists Housing Flea Market
why: Annual bag sale flea market at Westbeth Artists Housing with art, clothing, and objects.

name: Coltrane 100
why: Concert celebrating the 100th anniversary of John Coltrane's birth.

name: Yoshitomo Nara Exhibition
why: Solo exhibition of paintings and sculptures by Japanese artist Yoshitomo Nara; runs through December 12.

name: 15th Annual Gotham Storytelling Festival
source: Gotham Center for New York City History
why: Annual festival featuring live storytelling performances across New York City; runs through November 15.

name: Stanley Wolukau-Wanambwa: Henry Wolf Chair in Photography Artist Talk
why: Fall 2026 Henry Wolf Chair in Photography Stanley Wolukau-Wanambwa discusses the role of order in his practice as artist and critic, in conversation with Associate Curator Phil Taylor of the George Eastman Museum.

name: Public Art Fund Talks: Camille Henrot
venue: Frederick P. Rose Auditorium, Cooper Union
why: Artist Camille Henrot discusses Dogs, her first solo public exhibition in NYC at Doris C. Freedman Plaza, featuring new dog sculptures exploring domestication, care, and social codes.

name: Mark West: Seeing Things, Pareidolia and the Discovery of Form
why: Architect Mark West presents techniques of 'hallucinatory' drawing using pareidolia, structural form-finding with flexible materials, and sculptural discovery as alternatives to methods of control.

name: David Hume Kennerly: In the Room — Sixty Years on the Front Line of History
why: Pulitzer Prize-winning photographer David Hume Kennerly—former White House photographer for President Ford—discusses 60 years of iconic images from RFK's assassination to the Vietnam War, in conversation with ABC News historian Mark K. Updegrove.

name: MAS Tour: Grand Central Terminal
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
via: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: Ongoing guided architectural and historical tours of Grand Central Terminal led by MAS docents, mostly indoors.

name: MAS Tour: Tenement Historic District — History of Housing in Yorkville
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
via: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: Walking tour of Yorkville's tenement historic district exploring the history of working-class housing in NYC, led by James Russiello.

name: MAS Tour: Histories of Social Housing
source: Municipal Art Society of New York
via: Municipal Art Society of New York
why: Walking tour examining the history and architecture of public and social housing in New York City, led by Katelin Penner.

name: Holiday Express: Toys and Trains from the Jerni Collection
why: Annual wintertime exhibition featuring model trains, toy stations, and miniatures illustrating design evolution from early 20th century to WWII era; opens November 13.

name: Friday Night Fever!
why: DJ Kultured Child (SiriusXM host Angélika Beener) spins 70s and 80s disco and hip hop classics in the You Should Be Dancing: New York, 1976 and Beyond exhibition.

name: Designing Women Market
why: Curated marketplace showcasing jewelry, textiles, accessories, and crafts by women makers and designers.

name: Primary Source: McDarrah at 100
why: Panel discussion on photojournalist Fred W. McDarrah, the first staff photographer for The Village Voice, who documented NYC counterculture and social change over six decades.

name: Roundtable with the Lenape Center
venue: Brooklyn Public Library Central Branch, Dweck Center
why: Roundtable on the 1778 Treaty with the Delaware and its aftermath, featuring the Lenape Center's Joe Baker and Hadrien Coumans, law professor Nicholas Robinson, and moderator Joseph T. Murphy.

name: Classical Interludes: Joao Luiz Rezende
venue: Brooklyn Public Library Central Branch, Dweck Center
why: Two-time Latin Grammy nominee guitarist Joao Luiz Rezende performs solo guitar spanning classical, Brazilian, and world music from Dowland to Berio.

name: Navigating Perimenopause with Clarity
why: Physician-led talk covering what happens hormonally during perimenopause and practical approaches to supporting hormones and the nervous system.

name: Greenpoint Bike Clinic: Free Repair and Maintenance
why: Free bike repair pop-up with Greenpoint Bike Clinic: basic tune-ups, flat repairs, and brake/shifter adjustments. Also Nov 21.

name: Printmaking Workshop
why: Hands-on printmaking session covering foundations and ink transfer inspired by traditional Asian artisanry; materials provided.

name: Dialog Without Words: Art Exhibition by Irina Dzevel
why: Opening reception for an intimate exhibition of paintings by Irina Dzevel at Coney Island Library, curated by Boris Ioselev.

name: Astronomy Night: Sidewalk Stargazing
why: Evening sidewalk stargazing session identifying what's visible in an urban environment with light pollution.

name: Street Tree Care with Big Reuse
why: Hands-on neighborhood tree bed care workshop with Big Reuse; all supplies provided.

name: 23rd PowerUP Business Plan Competition Awards Ceremony
venue: Brooklyn Public Library Central Branch, Dweck Center
why: Annual celebration awarding over $40,000 in cash and prizes to Brooklyn small business competition winners, with food, refreshments, and a holiday market.

name: Vitality Arts (Ages 55+): Makers' Lab
why: Hands-on art-making workshop in the galleries for adults 55 and older; runs Nov 12–13.

name: ASL Tour: Iris van Herpen
why: ASL-interpreted tour of the Iris van Herpen: Sculpting the Senses exhibition, led by a Deaf/hard-of-hearing guide.

name: Museum on Wheels: Roebling Rink
why: Brooklyn Museum brings art activities and programs to Roebling Rink at Brooklyn Bridge Park.

name: Brooklyn Mornings: Art of Manga
why: Guided 90-minute tour of the Art of Manga exhibition for adults, exploring how manga has shaped global visual culture.

name: Salsa Party at the Brooklyn Museum
why: Evening salsa dancing party at the Brooklyn Museum.

name: Build City x NEAR Legion: NEAR Private AI Hackathon NYC
why: Full-day hackathon building AI apps on private inference with NEAR AI Cloud and Trusted Execution Environments, eligible for $250,000 global prize pool.

name: World of Tavily NYC
why: Immersive evening on how production AI agents find and use live web information, with lightning talks from Tavily, Nebius, and LangChain.

name: Durable AI Workflows with Temporal and MongoDB
why: Talks and demos on AI workflows that recover gracefully from failures, covering RAG with MongoDB Atlas and agent coordination with Temporal.

name: Gemini 4 NYC Hackathon
why: Cerebral Valley + Google DeepMind hackathon with $20,000 in prizes across tracks spanning advanced reasoning, visual coding, robotics, and world models.

name: AI Dev / New York City: Andrew Ng's AI Developer Conference
why: Two-day AI conference hosted by Andrew Ng with speakers from Yann LeCun, OpenAI, BlackRock, Hugging Face, and Stanford on frontier models, agentic coding, and deploying AI in production; runs Nov 30–Dec 1.

name: Lakeside Ice Skating at Prospect Park
venue: LeFrak Center at Lakeside, Prospect Park
why: Seasonal ice skating on covered and open-air rinks at Prospect Park's LeFrak Center at Lakeside, with figure skating and ice hockey classes and leagues.

name: New Year's Eve Fireworks in Prospect Park
why: 46th annual New Year's Eve celebration in Prospect Park with live entertainment starting at 10 pm and fireworks at midnight.

name: From Field to Form: Ocean Flora
venue: The Architectural League of New York
price: $20 general / Free for League members and Parsons students
why: Expert panel on the use of marine organisms—including seaweed and sea mosses—as sustainable building materials, exploring ocean flora's potential in architecture.

name: After Hours: INC Architecture & Design
why: Exclusive behind-the-scenes studio visit to INC Architecture & Design's downtown New York office for Architectural League members.

name: Current Work | Forms of Intelligence: Labor
venue: The Architectural League of New York
price: $20 general / Free for League members and Cooper Union students
why: In-person lecture on labor, intelligence, and the built environment, with CEUs available for architects and design professionals.

name: After Hours: Arup
why: Final studio visit of the season: an exclusive after-hours tour of Arup's New York office, the global engineering and built environment consultancy founded in 1946.

name: Correspondences: de Appel 1975–2025 — Opening Conversation
why: Opening conversation with curators and archivists exploring 50 years of correspondence from the de Appel art institute archive, with Jeremy Johnston, Ben DuVall, Martha Jager, Nell Donkers, and Rachel Churner; archival display runs through Nov 20.

name: Listfulness: A Poetry Writing Workshop
why: Afternoon poetry writing workshop exploring the list as a form, led by Printed Matter.

name: Back to the Present: 50 Years of Free Expression with Franklin Furnace
why: Celebration and conversation marking 50 years of Franklin Furnace's advocacy for free expression in avant-garde art.

name: Eric Copeland on Demon Portraits with Dem Passwords — Book Launch
why: Book launch event with musician and artist Eric Copeland discussing Demon Portraits with Dem Passwords.

name: Tellus Audio Cassette Magazine Anthology Vol. 1 — Listening Session & Conversation
why: Communal listening session and discussion around the Tellus Audio Cassette Magazine Anthology, celebrating the legendary 1980s–90s avant-garde cassette journal that released work by Laurie Anderson, John Cage, and Sonic Youth.

name: Subway Swing: A Boogie for the Ages
why: Annual after-hours dance party in the Museum's 1936 decommissioned subway station, featuring live jazz by Charlie Caranicas & The Lean Mean Swing Machine, Kayla Lewis and the Krewe de Klew, and the Hyuna Park Trio; beginner swing lesson included; complimentary maple Old Fashioned.

name: "Made in New York" Filmmaker Listening Tour
why: NYC Mayor's Office of Media and Entertainment's first 'Made in NY' Filmmaker Listening Tour, hosted by Queens World Film Festival as part of the First Amendment Film & Arts Festival at MoMI.

name: Fall Yoga with The Yoga Room at MoMI
why: Free weekly Sunday yoga class at MoMI with local studio The Yoga Room; continues through Dec 27.

name: MoMI After Dark Tours
why: Guided lantern tour through MoMI's Behind the Screen galleries focusing on the spooky side of film and TV history—including props from The Exorcist and The Silence of the Lambs; also Nov 28.

name: MoMI Merch Meet
why: MoMI's first artisan market showcasing creative expressions of love for the moving image from local makers—art, hats, shirts, buttons, jewelry, zines, comics, housewares, and more; runs until 6pm.

name: Lightscape at Brooklyn Botanic Garden
why: Spectacular new illuminated trail through the Garden celebrating its four seasons, with luminous installations and light-kissed landscapes; presented in partnership with Sony Music and ConEd. Opens Nov 20, runs through early January.

name: Starting Seeds for Community Self-Sufficiency
why: Seasoned community garden leader shares tips for seed-saving success, covering basics of selecting, harvesting, and storing seeds for year-round community food production.

name: Nature-Inspired Clay Magnets Workshop
why: Hands-on workshop drawing inspiration from local plants and flowers to sculpt and shape air-dry clay into 8-10 unique magnets to take home.

name: Changing Tastes: American Foodways at 250
why: Top Chef semi-finalist Lana Lagomarsini and food historian Jane Ziegelman discuss American foodways through immigrant and Black American culinary traditions, including 97 Orchard and Edna Lewis's The Taste of Country Cooking.

name: Affordable Housing Conference with Believe New York
why: NYC affordable housing conference with Believe New York, NYC Housing Connect, and Fair Housing Justice Center—speakers, workshops, and over 15 partner organizations to answer questions about housing opportunities and tenant rights; runs until 3pm.

name: The Next Century of Black Studies Conference
venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
source: New York Public Library / Schomburg Center
why: Three-day conference convening scholars, graduate students, community archivists, and public historians to explore frontiers of Black Studies and the next century of the field; runs Nov 16-18 at the Schomburg Center.

name: Get Lit Book Club: Ply by Hernan Diaz with WNYC
why: Special in-person event with Pulitzer Prize-winning author Hernan Diaz discussing his newest novel Ply, hosted by WNYC's Alison Stewart; free with Get Lit Book Club access to the novel throughout November.

name: Joanna Jackson Goldman Memorial Lectures: Native Nations & the American Revolution
why: Historian Ned Blackhawk delivers a two-part biennial lecture on Benjamin Franklin's origins, Native American communities, and their influence on the American Revolution; Part I Nov 17, Part II Nov 18, each requiring separate registration.

name: Between the Lines: Between the River & the Railroad Tracks by Nicole R. Fleetwood
venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
source: New York Public Library / Schomburg Center
why: Launch celebration and conversation for NYPL and MacArthur Fellow Nicole R. Fleetwood's debut memoir about family memory and the Black Midwest, moderated by Hanif Abdurraqib; reception and book signing follow.

name: Screening & Discussion: The Drug in Our Pocket
why: Screening of documentary clips from The Drug in Our Pocket, followed by a panel discussion on digital technology's impact on youth mental health with Dr. Aliza Pressman, Tali Horowitz, and others; light bites provided.

name: Eiko Ishibashi: GIFT
why: Acclaimed Japanese multi-instrumentalist Eiko Ishibashi performs live to visuals from Drive My Car director Ryusuke Hamaguchi in this Durations Festival collaboration with Public Records; one-night-only performance.

name: Terence Tao: Six Math Essentials
why: Fields Medalist and 'Mozart of mathematics' Terence Tao joins Pioneer Works' Director of Sciences Janna Levin to celebrate his first popular book, Six Math Essentials, exploring algebra, geometry, uncertainty, and the mathematics of change. (Sold out—check for returns.)

name: Rachel Cusk: Life of M
why: In collaboration with The Yale Review, Meghan O'Rourke interviews Rachel Cusk about Life of M, her autofiction on fame, identity, and movie stardom—the author's only U.S. event for the book.

name: Continuing Education: Energy Build
why: Artist Alex Dolores Salerno leads Energy Build, a political experiment in self-care as collective care—drawing on the concept of an art build to collectively construct energy for artists, organizers, activists, and advocates.

name: Immigrant Nation: Making Home in Song and Story
why: David Goren and Maria Margaronis explore how immigrants used music, skits, and recorded messages—from Ellis Island to the present—to connect with home and find community; archival recordings from the Library for Arts & Culture collection.

name: Helen Tworkov, Cyrus Dunham & Oneika Mays on Buddhism in America
why: Helen Tworkov, founder of Tricycle: The Buddhist Review, in conversation with writer Cyrus Dunham and meditation instructor Oneika Mays about the challenges and gifts of Buddhism in America today.

name: Forgotten History: The Brooklyn Theater Fire of 1876
why: Marking the 150th anniversary of one of NYC's deadliest disasters, authors Arthur Scinta and Melanie Gall reconstruct the 1876 Brooklyn Theater fire and Gilded Age theater culture using CBH archival materials; moderated by chief historian Dominique Jean-Louis.

name: RestFest Film Festival: Short Films by Disabled & Mad Artists
why: Screening of short films and video art by Crip, Disabled, Deaf, Chronically Ill, Neurodivergent, and Mad artists from the artist-run RestFest Film Festival; works also streamable online for a limited time after the event.

name: Layli Long Soldier Discusses 'We' with Fred Moten
why: Poet Layli Long Soldier discusses We, an arrangement of poems, lyric essays, and visual art, in conversation with critical theorist and poet Fred Moten—a rare pairing of two essential voices in contemporary poetry.

name: Sea Stories 2026 at The Explorers Club
why: Annual all-day ocean exploration symposium at the Explorers Club HQ on E 70th Street, featuring presentations on Arctic/Antarctic diving, cave exploration, a lost F4U Corsair off NJ, and the future of aquariums; breakfast, lunch, and cocktail party included.

name: Hand-Sewn Mini Quilt Workshop
why: Brand-new 3-hour beginner workshop covering piecing, assembling, hand-quilting, and finishing a mini quilt; take home a finished piece from this cozy Greenpoint studio (165 Greenpoint Ave).

name: Knitting 102: Billie Bandana
why: Intermediate knitting workshop to make a stylish Billie Bandana at Brooklyn Craft Company in Greenpoint; a second session runs Dec 10.

name: Needle Felted Pets Workshop
why: Evening workshop to sculpt a miniature felted version of your pet (or any animal!) using needle-felting techniques at Brooklyn Craft Co.'s Greenpoint studio.

name: Make a Holiday Wreath
why: Seasonal wreath-making workshop at Brooklyn Craft Co.'s Greenpoint Annex; multiple sessions available through Dec 11—perfect holiday project to brighten your space.

name: The Occupied City: New York and the American Revolution
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Major immersive exhibition spanning MCNY's entire third floor, tracing New York's choices, conflicts, and consequences from 1763 to 1790 through historical objects, interactive environments, and multimedia; developed in partnership with the Gotham Center for NYC History.

name: Underground NYC Tour: Subway 101
venue: New York Transit Museum (off-site subway tour)
why: Expert-guided subway tour visiting stations old and new, exploring secrets of the system, art, architecture, and exclusive archival images from the Transit Museum collection—a great deep-dive for city history fans.

name: Transit Walk: Second Avenue's Art and Transit History
why: Walking tour tracing Second Avenue's transit history from trolley kiosk on the Queensboro Bridge through today's subway, including site-specific artworks by Jean Shin, Vik Muniz, and Sarah Sze—led by NYTM expert guides.

name: Transit Walk: Art and Design Secrets of Penn Station & Moynihan Train Hall
why: Expert-guided walking tour uncovering hidden Beaux-Arts remnants of the original Penn Station (1910), through Moynihan Train Hall's new public art—a rare architectural and transit history experience; second session same day at 2pm.

name: How To Build A Black Hole
why: Silke Weinfurtner, Chair of the CERN Quantum Technology Initiative and Professor of Quantum at the University of Manchester, presents a lecture on how to build a black hole at the Simons Foundation.

name: NASA Space Apps Hackathon
why: Annual NASA-led global hackathon with NYC host at NYU Tandon, challenging teams to use NASA's open data to tackle real problems on Earth and in space—one of the world's largest hackathons.

name: Asian Tech Week NYC
why: Community-led initiative bringing together founders, builders, investors, operators, creatives, and leaders shaping the future of tech; runs Nov 16-20 with events across the city—anyone can host an event.

name: Engineering for Humanity
why: Gerald Chan (Founder, Morningside Group) joins Columbia for a talk on Engineering for Humanity—the intersection of technology, global health, and human development.

name: Yoshitomo Nara at David Zwirner
why: New exhibition of work by beloved Japanese artist Yoshitomo Nara at David Zwirner's Chelsea gallery; known for his melancholic, wide-eyed children and dogs—closes Dec 12.

name: Red Hook Defiant: Revolutionary War Walking Tour
venue: Red Hook Interim Library (362 Van Brunt St)
why: Brainery teacher and tour guide Daniel Pecoraro leads a first-run walking tour of Red Hook's role in the Battle of Brooklyn, tracing Fort Defiance, harbor defense sites, and revolutionary memorials; tour ends at Valentino Pier. Email jen@brooklynbrainery.com to RSVP.
